title: Residensi Alamanda: RM300,000 affordable homes next to Bangsar South.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #411 | RESIDENSI ALAMANDA, PANTAI SENTRAL PARK
excerpt: A newly handed-over Rumawip block built alongside a private project near Bangsar South, at RM300,000 a unit. Sean calls the location and value hard to beat, but flags the entrance, the gym and the coming density.
takeaways: Every three-bedroom unit costs about RM300,000, whatever the floor or view.
Estimated rent of about RM2,000 to RM2,200 against an instalment of about RM1,300 plus fees.
Resale is restricted for five to ten years, and the entrance is cramped and unsafe for pedestrians.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Residensi Alamanda is a Rumawip block of about 600 units that a developer must build before its higher-priced project next door, with buyers limited by income. Each floor has 22 units of a single type and two lift cores with two passenger lifts and a fire lift each. The level-six deck has a lap pool and wading pool with an infinity edge, a small jacuzzi, a playground, a games room and reading room, and a rooftop stargazing deck is being finished.

Sean viewed a top-floor three-bedroom, two-bathroom unit with a ceiling of about 2.9 m, a long kitchen with a yard, a 4 m-wide living room with an awkward route past the bedroom doors, heavily tinted windows and a master bedroom with its own bathroom. Fittings are simpler than open-market units: smaller doors, fewer sockets and steel railings.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: Pantai Sentral Park lies at the end of Bangsar South near the MPE highway, behind Bukit Gasing, which separates it from PJ. The Federal Highway, Old Klang Road, KL Eco City and Bangsar South's offices, malls and LRT are close, and the master plan's roads and pavements are already finished. Around the site are a cemetery, village houses, a car dump, construction sites and a well-kept sewage treatment plant.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Units cost about RM300,000 regardless of floor. Sean estimates rent at about RM2,000 to RM2,200 against an instalment of about RM1,300 plus RM150 to RM200 in maintenance; the buyers he met found no rental restriction in their agreements. Resale is barred for five to ten years, whereas an open-market unit nearby costs about RM150,000 more and rents for more.

standout.title: Glass-roofed voids
standout.body: A tinted glass roof covers every internal void, so rain can't fall into the corridors or the bathrooms and rooms that open onto them, while daylight still comes through. It solves a common source of leaks and mess in affordable blocks with a simple, inexpensive detail.

pros: The location: Federal Highway, MPE and Old Klang Road, Bangsar South and KL Eco City next door, plenty of well-paid jobs nearby, and views of Bukit Gasing or the city skyline. He nearly paid RM800,000 to RM1 million for a project opposite.
The value: about RM300,000 for any floor, renting for an estimated RM2,000 to RM2,200 against an instalment of about RM1,300, so he urges anyone who qualifies to buy a Rumawip first.
The common facilities and build: an infinity-edge pool, jacuzzi, playground, furnished reading room and gym, a rooftop deck, six lifts for 22 units a floor, and tidy, solid construction.
cons: The micro setting: a high-density project next door, a car dump and future development in front, and the sewage plant behind, though he noticed no smell or noise inside.
Density will rise: four or five projects of 1,000 to 2,000 units each are under way, although open-market neighbours at double the price should keep demand for cheaper units.

Design issues: a cramped entrance with no pedestrian walkway, no proper loading bay, no transfer structure, so the gym is squeezed into what should have been units, and uneven finishing between showy and bare areas.

closing: One of the best-located affordable homes in KL; if you qualify, Sean says buy it, and just choose your view carefully.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this November 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The owner, a former podcast guest, let Sean view the unit just after handover; the price is the owner's, and the rent and instalment are Sean's estimates. Rumawip eligibility, resale and rental rules vary, so check them before buying.
